meta.decision_note: Angle is right. Keep the clinical tone light, this is not a medical page.

page.h1: How to stop procrastinating with ADHD when starting is the hard part

angle.why_this_page_exists: Every page ranking for this explains the neuroscience of why ADHD procrastination happens and then stops, leaving the reader informed and still stuck. This one gives the mechanism in two paragraphs and spends the rest on what to do in the next ten minutes.
gaps_to_exploit: None of the top four give a concrete first action for the next ten minutes
None address the capture problem, that the task is often not written down anywhere
The two highest ranking pages carry no images at all, so the pages are a wall of text
No page in the top ten runs an FAQ, despite four People Also Ask boxes on the SERP
angle.differentiation: Clinical publishers cannot recommend a specific workflow without hedging. We can be concrete, and we concede where medication or therapy is the real answer.

competitors.notable: Strong on the why, ten H2 sections, but every suggestion is a general principle rather than a step.
Thin at under 1,000 words, and its images are icons and stock rather than anything explanatory.
Best structured of the three. Bot-blocked, so read via WebFetch.

structure.opening: Open on the specific moment: the task is known, the deadline is real, and the person still cannot start. Name it in two sentences, then answer. No definition of ADHD first.
